summary.title: Seven habits of effective text editing 2.0
summary.one_liner: A 2007 Google talk by Vim author Bram Moolenaar showing, through seven worked examples, how to spot repeated editing inefficiencies, find a quicker Vim command, and turn it into a habit.
keywords: seven habits of effective text editing
star command search word under cursor
takeaways: Use a three-step loop: detect an inefficient repeated action, find a quicker command (ask colleagues, read help, check the mailing list), then make it a habit.
Vim's * command and the hlsearch option make finding variable and function usages faster than typing each search.
Insert mode completion (CTRL-N/CTRL-P) avoids retyping long identifiers, and omni-completion in Vim 7.0 adds context-sensitive matches.
Automatic spelling correction via abbreviations or spell-check mappings removes repeated manual fixes for common typos.
Investing time in learning editor commands pays off when you edit text for much of your day.
summary.summary: This is a slide deck (converted to PDF) from a presentation Bram Moolenaar gave at Google in February 2007. It argues that people spend much of their day editing text and that learning an editor's features is worth the effort. The talk is organised around a method of detecting inefficiency, finding a quicker way, and making it a habit, with examples covering search, identifier completion, spell correction, and file navigation. The examples are Vim-specific, and the deck ends partway through the fourth habit about navigating between files.
